The 2026 Ohio gubernatorial election will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the governor of Ohio. Republican entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy and Democratic former state health director Amy Acton are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican incumbent governor Mike DeWine is ineligible to seek a third consecutive term.

Primary elections were held on May 5, with Ramaswamy defeating minimal opposition for the Republican nomination and Acton running unopposed for the Democratic nomination. If elected, Ramaswamy would become the first Indian American governor of Ohio and the first Hindu governor in the United States.[a] Acton would be Ohio's first elected female[b] and first Jewish governor if elected.

The campaign has been described as "ugly" and heavily reliant on negative campaigning. Ramaswamy has focused on Acton's background to portray her as dishonest and mentally ill, while Acton has portrayed Ramaswamy as an out-of-touch plutocrat and con artist.[1]

Democrats have not won a gubernatorial election in Ohio since 2006. The winner of the election will be inaugurated on January 11, 2027.[2]

Campaign

[edit]

On September 2, Ramaswamy accepted invitations to participate in gubernatorial debates hosted by CNN and WLWT and called on Acton to join him. Acton's campaign subsequently declined, citing what it characterized as inaccurate and personal attacks in Ramaswamy's campaign advertising. As a result, no debates between the two major-party nominees have been scheduled.[133]

Canfield Fair incident

[edit]

On September 6, Acton was attacked at a campaign event at the Canfield Fair. An armed individual lunged at her and was apprehended by local authorities. Several campaign volunteers suffered minor injuries.[134] The suspect, Patrick Havas, was charged with "two counts of assault and one count of disorderly conduct."[135]

Attacks on Amy Acton's upbringing & ad controversy

[edit]

The Ramaswamy campaign has been described as "ugly" and heavily focused upon negative campaigning.[136]

Attack ads by the Vivek Ramaswamy campaign focused on Acton's background to portray her as dishonest and mentally ill,[137][138] claiming that she had "lied" and "exaggerated" about being abused, despite evidence that she had undergone childhood rape, other types of sexual abuse, homelessness, poverty, and parental neglect.[137][138][139]

An attack ad featuring Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, denouncing her received nationwide attention. Arthur has been estranged from Acton since Acton was removed from her stepfather's and her mother's home at the age of 12; the stepfather was charged with raping her.[136][138][139] The ad was initially only shared on social media and lacked a "paid for by" television disclosure; the Ramaswamy campaign later took credit for creating it.[140] Connie Luck, a spokesperson for Ramaswamy’s campaign, said the ad will "air both online and on TV in the closing days of the campaign". On October 21, 2026, the Ramaswamy campaign said it would broadcast the ad, despite the $4 million price tag and bipartisan condemnation.[137] Ohio Republicans, including U.S. Senator Jon Husted and Secretary of State Frank LaRose, publicly criticized the ad.[141] Two days later, Governor Mike DeWine called for the ad to be pulled.[142] President Trump expressed support for the ad, encouraging Ramaswamy to keep running it, and criticized DeWine for his opposition.[143] Vice President Vance also expressed support for the ad.[144]

The Associated Press reported that Acton's brother, Philip Stearns, "said the two were removed from their mother Donna Arthur’s custody as children after their stepfather, Arthur’s husband, was indicted for raping Acton as a child. Acton has not seen Arthur, whose last known address was in Pennsylvania, since they were in a courtroom together in 1978. According to police and court documents obtained by the Associated Press, Cledith Arthur was arrested and charged with the rape of his stepdaughter, then 12, in July 1978, after Acton’s biological father reported his alleged conduct to authorities. The abuse allegedly happened from December 1976 to April 1978. He was indicted by a grand jury that September, but failed to show at a court hearing and remained a fugitive until at least 1981. He has since died."[137]
